versions.name: Camp Mountain Run

features.note: Two-person canvas tents with cots on wooden platforms.
Most campsites include an Adirondack shelter.
Most campsites have space to hang hammocks.
The Eynon and Glen Ru cabins.
Individual shower stalls at the pool and at the Walker Center.
The Reitz Chapel, used for vespers.
Walker Pavilion.
An activity field, a parade field, and a volleyball court.
The Stackpole-Hall swimming pool.
Open swim, instructional swim, and a Mile Swim award.
Boone Lake.
A stocked fishing pond and a lake, supplied by a cooperative trout hatchery.
A black-powder version of the rifle programme.
An evening cowboy action shoot with rifle, shotgun, and pistol.
Troop COPE sessions on the low elements, plus open climb evenings.
Trailblazers, for Scouts in their first week of long-term camp.
Trailblazers hike out to a secluded part of the property to camp and cook.
Individual Scouts can join a provisional troop run by camp staff.
Mountain Adventure Camp, for Scouts fourteen and older.
Backpacking and a 50-Miler award within Mountain Adventure Camp.

versions.summary: Bucktail Council's 380-acre Scouts BSA resident camp in Penfield, Pennsylvania.

provenance.notes: Imported from camp-finder; raw description and sessions dropped (operational data stays at the council site). verified_at is camp-finder's own source-confirmation date; imported_at is when open-scout-api ingested it. The evergreen summary is original prose regenerated from that description, excluding dates/fees/schedules. camp_type classified from program_types. Features surveyed 2026-07-25 against the council's own camp page (that page is explicitly not an exhaustive activity list, so absence of a code is not evidence of absence). The stored council camping page is thin, so the linked Camp Mountain Run leader guide was read as the second source.
